checkers.customDescription: Custom checker {{name}} from the problem directory. JudgeDesk accepts C++ (.cpp) and Python (.py) sources; .exe files are not supported.

C1.title: C1LinesWordsIgnoreCase
C1.description: The files match when their ordered lists of lines and the ordered words on every line match, ignoring letter case and extra word separators. Extra blank lines at the end do not change the result, but a blank line at the beginning does.

C2.title: C2LinesWordsCase
C2.description: The comparison is the same as C1LinesWordsIgnoreCase, but word matching is case-sensitive.

C3.title: C3WordsIgnoreCase
C3.description: The files match when their complete ordered lists of words match without regard to case. Words may be separated by spaces or placed on different lines without changing the result.

C4.title: C4WordsCase
C4.description: The comparison is the same as C3WordsIgnoreCase, but word matching is case-sensitive.

C5.title: C5Binary
C5.description: Suitable for every output file type. The checker compares the contestant file and answer file byte by byte and reports the first differing byte or a different file length.

fcmp.title: fcmp.cpp
fcmp.description: Compares the files as a sequence of lines. Every character inside each expected line, including spaces and tabs, must match exactly.

hcmp.title: hcmp.cpp
hcmp.description: Compares one arbitrarily large signed decimal integer. The canonical form is required: zero is 0, and other values cannot contain a plus sign or leading zeroes.

lcmp.title: lcmp.cpp
lcmp.description: Compares a sequence of lines, treating each line as a sequence of tokens. Spacing inside a line is ignored, but moving a token to another line changes the result.

ncmp.title: ncmp.cpp
ncmp.summary: One or more int64, ignores whitespaces
ncmp.description: Compares ordered sequences of signed 64-bit integers. Whitespace between numbers is ignored; values and sequence length must match.

nyesno.title: nyesno.cpp
nyesno.description: Compares a sequence containing zero or more YES/NO tokens without regard to case. Invalid tokens are reported as presentation errors.

rcmp4.title: rcmp4.cpp
rcmp4.description: Compares a sequence of floating-point values with maximum absolute or relative error 1E-4, using Testlib double comparison semantics.

rcmp6.title: rcmp6.cpp
rcmp6.description: Compares a sequence of floating-point values with maximum absolute or relative error 1E-6, using Testlib double comparison semantics.

rcmp9.title: rcmp9.cpp
rcmp9.description: Compares a sequence of floating-point values with maximum absolute or relative error 1E-9, using Testlib double comparison semantics.

wcmp.title: wcmp.cpp
wcmp.description: Compares the complete ordered token sequence. All whitespace characters are separators and are otherwise ignored.

yesno.title: yesno.cpp
yesno.description: Compares one YES or NO token without regard to case. Invalid contestant tokens are presentation errors.

resourceOnly.title: Advanced: local toolchains with resource-only protection
resourceOnly.description: Enable this only when a local toolchain cannot run under strict isolation. JudgeDesk still enforces time, memory and process limits and cleans up the process tree, but the computer's filesystem and network are no longer isolated from executed code.
resourceOnly.enabled: Enabled. Compatible local toolchains may run with resource-only protection.
resourceOnly.disabled: Off (recommended). JudgeDesk accepts only managed packages or local toolchains that pass strict isolation compatibility.
resourceOnly.recovery: The saved policy file was invalid, so JudgeDesk disabled this mode.
resourceOnly.confirm:
Enable less-secure local execution?

JudgeDesk will still enforce time, memory and process limits, but it will not isolate the filesystem or network from compiling/executed code. Use this only on a trusted contest computer and prefer a JudgeDesk-managed package whenever possible.

setup.title: Compiler Setup Wizard
setup.subtitle: Configure compiler toolchains and Python runtimes for local offline grading.
setup.bothDesc: Installs C/C++ (GCC 14.2) and Python 3.12 isolated runtimes (about 195 MB download).
setup.bothDescMac: Uses the system Apple Clang compiler and installs an isolated Python 3.12 runtime.
setup.cppDesc: Installs the g++ compiler (GCC 14.2) toolchain (150 MB download).
setup.cppDescMac: Uses Apple Clang from Xcode Command Line Tools already installed on this Mac.
setup.pythonDesc: Installs the standalone Python 3.12 interpreter (about 45 MB download).
setup.judgerDesc: Skips downloads. JudgeDesk detects C/C++/Python from PATH at startup. A local installation becomes ready after its strict compatibility probe unless you explicitly enable the less-safe mode in Toolchain Manager.
setup.managedPythonNotice: Local Python can run submissions and custom checkers when its compatibility probe passes. A JudgeDesk-managed Python package remains the more predictable, strongly isolated choice for contests.
